title: Homily XXIII
subtitle: Matthew VII. 1.
author: chrysostom
excerpt: Homily XXIII. Matt. VII. 1. “Judge not, that ye be not judged.” What then? Ought we not to blame them that sin? Because Paul also saith this selfsame thing: or rather, there too it is Christ, speaking by Paul, and saying,Rom. xiv. 10.“Why dost thou judge thy brother? And thou, why dost thou set at nought thy brother?” and, “Who art thou that judgest another man’s servant?”Rom. xiv. 4. And again, “Therefore judge nothing before the time, until the Lord come.”1 Cor. iv. 5. How then doth He say elsewhere, “Reprove, rebuke, exhort,”2 Tim. iv. 2.and, “Them that sin rebuke before all?”1 Tim. v. 20. [R.V., “reprove.” The Greek verb is the same in Matt. xviii. 15 also.—R.] And Christ too to Peter, “Go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone,” and if he neglect to hear, add to thyself another also; and if not even so doth he yield, declare it to the church likewise?”Matt. xviii. 15, 16, 17. And how hath He set over us so many to reprove; and not only to reprove, but also to punish? For him that hearkens to none of these, He hath commanded to be “as a heathen man...
